content: This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, it is important to be aware of the following: 1. Severe Intestinal Condition: This medication may rarely cause a serious intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Symptoms may include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or blood/mucus in the stool. Contact your doctor immediately if these symptoms occur. 2. Fungal Infections: Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Notify your doctor if you notice white patches in your mouth, a change in vaginal discharge, or other signs of a fungal infection. 3. Allergic Reactions: Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but can occur. Symptoms may include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience these symptoms. 4. Heart Rhythm Changes (QT Prolongation): Moxifloxacin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. This can lead to serious (rarely fatal) fast/irregular heartbeat and other symptoms such as severe dizziness or fainting. The risk may be higher if you have certain medical conditions (e.g., low potassium or magnesium levels, heart disease) or are taking other medications that can prolong the QT interval. Inform your doctor of your medical history and all medications you are taking. 5. Blood Sugar Changes: This medication may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, especially in individuals with diabetes. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and report any symptoms of high blood sugar (e.g., increased thirst or urination) or low blood sugar (e.g., sudden sweating, shaking, fast heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands/feet). Carry glucose tablets or a quick source of sugar (e.g., candy, fruit juice) to treat low blood sugar if needed. 6. Dizziness and Impaired Alertness: Moxifloxacin may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. 7. Sun Sensitivity: This medication may make you more sensitive to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. 8. Vaccines: Moxifloxacin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccines. 9. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Use this medication during pregnancy only if clearly needed, as its effects on an unborn baby are not fully known. It is also unclear if this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. 10. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 11. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 8 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 12. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. 13. Overdose: In case of overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 14. Laboratory Monitoring: While taking this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., liver function tests, complete blood count, blood glucose levels) to monitor your response to treatment. Keep all medical and lab appointments. 15. Important Usage Information: This medication is prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Completing the full prescribed course is essential, even if symptoms improve after a few days, to prevent the infection from returning or worsening. 16. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, weakness, or trouble sleeping. If any of these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor promptly. 17. Tendon Damage and Nerve Problems: Quinolone antibiotics, including moxifloxacin, may cause serious and potentially permanent tendon damage (e.g., tendinitis, tendon rupture) and nerve problems (e.g., peripheral neuropathy). Tendon damage can occur during or after treatment. Stop exercising, rest, and seek medical help immediately if you develop joint/muscle/tendon pain or swelling. This medication may also worsen a muscle condition called myasthenia gravis. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
